A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 36-page versions of MetaMetrics. Their main text, Appendices A-H, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original MetaMetrics experiments across summarization, translation, question answering, image captioning and reward-model scoring, including correlations with human judgments, accuracy, ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results in Sections 5-6 and the appendices, including benchmark correlations and RewardBench accuracy.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices C-E retain the same GP-based Bayesian weighting, XGBoost, iterative feature pruning, objectives and preprocessing. No proposed procedure or component changes.

E1.justification: Both retain SummEval/BenchmarkLLM summarization, WMT translation, EQAE/EVOUNA question answering, Flickr8k/THumB captioning, and reward-model training and RewardBench evaluation. Cross-lingual and cross-dataset test coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Uniform and Weighted Avg rows added to appendix Tables 11, 12 and 14 reproduce the corresponding comparisons already reported in v3's main Tables 3, 2 and 4. The reported comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4's 30%/70% splits, benchmark-specific training and evaluation procedures, correlation and accuracy metrics, and settings in Appendices D-E are unchanged. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The weighting and correlation-objective ablations in Tables 15-16, cross-lingual and cross-dataset tests in Tables 17-19, runtime analysis in Table 20, and feature-importance analyses are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v4 introduces no uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and figure contents are unchanged; for example, MetaMetrics-RM GP retains 93.5% overall RewardBench accuracy. The additional ensemble rows in appendix Tables 11, 12 and 14 duplicate existing main-text results.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup in Section 3, alternative weighting in Appendix C, preprocessing equations in D, kernel formulation in E, and correlation definitions in H are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning supervised metric calibration, alignment with human preferences, flexibility across modalities and languages, and effectiveness across five tasks.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly states that exploration of RLHF with PPO is left to future studies, explicitly identifying an untested application. Existing resource limitations and interpretations of performance, interpretability and robustness remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Dataset sizes, preprocessing, GP/XGBoost hyperparameters, hardware, runtime details and code/model/data access information are unchanged. The runtime discussion is relocated without adding reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and reference list are unchanged. Appendix F.6 reformats existing GP citations into parenthetical form without adding literature or revising research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 adds ICLR 2025 publication wording and makes limited prose and citation-punctuation edits, including '27 billion' to '27B' and a short clarification in F.5. The section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Appendix Tables 11, 12 and 14 gain ensemble-baseline blocks displaying existing results, with adjusted highlighting and appendix reflow. Figures 5-7 move to later pages, but all eleven figure images are identical. Publication headers are added throughout.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves clarity: Appendix A explicitly reserves PPO-based RLHF for future work, and Tables 11, 12 and 14 place existing ensemble comparisons alongside detailed results. These changes improve scope qualification and appendix usability, while the methods and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
